terms.definition: The smallest unit of life that can carry out all the basic functions needed to stay alive.
A cell that keeps its DNA inside a nucleus wrapped in its own membrane, and has other membrane-bound organelles.
The thin, flexible outer boundary that controls what enters and leaves the cell.
The jelly-like fluid inside the cell membrane that holds and supports all the organelles.
The organelle that stores the cell's DNA and directs the cell's activities, like a control center.
The molecule that carries the coded instructions for building and running the cell, organized into genes.
An organelle that breaks down nutrients to produce usable energy (ATP) for the cell; often called the 'powerhouse.'
A tiny structure, free-floating or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum, that builds proteins by reading genetic instructions.
A network of folded membranes that helps build, fold, and transport proteins and lipids through the cell.
A stack of flattened sacs that packages, modifies, and ships proteins to their final destination.
A sac filled with enzymes that breaks down waste, worn-out parts, and unwanted material inside the cell.
A network of protein fibers that gives the cell its shape, holds organelles in place, and helps the cell move or divide.
A specialized structure inside a cell that performs a specific job, similar to how organs work in a body.
